primitives.assumptions: Assumes a deterministic, observable outcome space for each event.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when event outcomes are fundamentally non-deterministic or unverifiable.

layer2.mapping: The Signal Ledger implements a sequential Bayesian updating framework where each event record serves as a likelihood update on the posterior distribution of model performance. It mirrors the conformal prediction process used in Galaxy Sports Intelligence (GSI), treating each settlement as a new observation that recalibrates confidence intervals.
layer2.telemetry: Number of unique model versions with sufficient settlement history (>30) and their corresponding win-rates.

primitives.name: Confidence Calibration Delta
primitives.verbatim_quote: ; confidencePredicted: number; // 0–100, from pick generation confidenceCalibrationDelta: number; // Actual outcome vs.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes binary outcomes (win/loss) and that predicted probabilities are well-calibrated.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when the underlying model exhibits systematic bias or heteroskedasticity across different contexts.

layer2.mapping: The delta calculation is mathematically equivalent to the residual error in a probabilistic classification model. In GSI, this maps to the difference between predicted win-probabilities and realized outcomes, driving conformal prediction interval adjustments. In GSE, it informs state-transition probabilities for optimal resource allocation.
layer2.telemetry: Mean absolute delta per model version, stratified by confidence bins.

primitives.name: Append-Only Rule
primitives.verbatim_quote: Corrections are made by creating new entries with a reference to the entry being corrected.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes data immutability and referential integrity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the reference system cannot handle versioned pointers or if storage costs become prohibitive.

layer2.mapping: Enforces idempotent monoid structure on event logs, ensuring that cumulative information does not decrease over time. This is analogous to the martingale property in GSI, where no new information can reduce the expected value, and to state-machine replication in GSE, preventing inconsistent system states.
layer2.telemetry: Total number of event entries vs. total number of logical corrections (deletes).

primitives.name: Calibration Feedback Loop
primitives.verbatim_quote: --## Calibration Feedback Loop The ledger is the mechanism by which Sports OS becomes self-correcting: 1.
primitives.assumptions: Bayes' theorem holds, and all relevant data is captured in the ledger.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when dependencies between events violate conditional independence, leading to double-counting or omitted variable bias.

layer2.mapping: The loop implements recursive Bayes filtering, identical to the online learning algorithms in GSI. Each settlement updates the prior distribution, which then informs subsequent predictions. In GSE, this maps to adaptive policy optimization under uncertainty.
layer2.telemetry: Effective sample size of posterior distribution (number of equivalent independent samples).
